Colorado derives income each year of 5 to 7 million dollars from the sale of hunting and fishing licenses alone. I predict that this income will be effectively reduced by 85 percent within two years as a result of this order.
Location and development of much needed new mineral and petroleum resources are severely handicapped accordingly.
There are many all-terrain vehicles available which, because of their construction, virtually eliminate the possibility of terrain damage. The ground contact P.S.I. being 1/350 that of a horse. These apparently were not taken into consideration with the issuance of this order.
This literally forces off-road enthusiasts to streets and high-ways and probably will be reflected by a proportionate percentage increase in accident and fatality statistics.
The aged and infirm are pretty much left out of public land participation as a result.
There are many of us who, because of damages sustained in the battle against dictatorial oppression during World War II, do not go along with the aura surrounding this subject.
I personally believe that decisions such as these should be returned to the authority where they rightfully belong: The United States Congress.
Last year, Gordon Allott sent tapes to the regional radio stations proclaiming the Flat Tops area as a natural for inclusion into the wilderness because it was devoid of human development. In reality, the area has many rouds, etc., constructed under the authority of the Forest Service for the purpose of harvesting beetle-killed timber resulting from excessive predator control. This could have been a contributing factor in Allott's defeat because we are really not that stupid.
In no way do I feel that consideration should be extended for further land addition to the wilderness concept until Executive Order 11644 is rescinded.
Very truly yours,
R. H. Schif
172
